first.rationale: Verify the prior onboarding result because completion is currently declining and the evidence directly supports a reversible intervention tied to activation and time-to-value. Verify promotional pricing because competitor pressure makes it consequential, but discounting may reduce sustainable qualified revenue or attract lower-value accounts. Run a guarded onboarding simplification experiment measuring qualified activation, first meaningful action, retention proxies, and downstream pipeline—not completion alone.

final.rationale: Use the confirmed shortened-onboarding intervention this week. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline, with prior evidence of higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. Run a standard experiment with guardrails and evaluate qualified activation, first meaningful action, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and downstream qualified revenue rather than completion alone. Do not use promotional pricing: although it lifted short-term qualified revenue, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
